blast_radius: Spend only; the burn dimension never fails a loop on its own.

throughput.derivation: Read-only database query inside the service's own container over one SSH session. Aggregates call count, cost and tokens by day(created_at) across configured LLM providers; 24h window for the observed row.
notes: LLM error rate in 24h is effectively zero — the model layer is not the failure mode when downstream volume drops.

Across all providers the 24h picture (illustrative) is roughly 200,000 calls with a small non-ok share, split between auth errors and rate limits, concentrated in a couple of high-volume API endpoints.
Costs are read from provider_calls.cost_usd; no credential value is read.
throughput.signal_path: postgres://example-service-db/example_service (container-local; credentials in EXAMPLE_SERVICE_* env, never read by capmap)#provider_calls

verification.note: Graded on throughput, not liveness: a running loop with zero volume is DEGRADED.
verification.source: postgres://example-service-db/example_service (container-local; credentials in EXAMPLE_SERVICE_* env, never read by capmap)#provider_calls

what_it_does: LLM call layer for the support pipeline; volume is model calls, with cost and token burn recorded for audit.
why_it_matters: Confirms the loop is spending on inference at its normal rate — useful as a corroborating signal when a downstream stage reports zero output, because it separates 'the LLM stopped' from 'the LLM ran and the send stage dropped it'.
